source_text: FOREWORD
translated_text: 前言

source_text:
It is now fifty years since Interaction of Color was published and, almost immediately,
began to change the way people all over the world thought about seeing. Shortly after
it came out, it became a best-selling book, as it has been ever since. Its success is
easy to understand, for it brings infinite personal pleasure while perpetually
expanding the way that colors are used and perceived in art, architecture,
translated_text: 《色彩的相互作用》出版至今已有五十年，几乎在问世后不久，它便开始改变世界各地人们对于观看的思考方式。该书出版后不久即成为畅销书，此后一直如此。它的成功不难理解，因为它在带来无穷个人愉悦的同时，也不断扩展着色彩在艺术、建筑、

source_text:
textiles, interior design, and graphic media at every level of technology. Yet we
should not forget that when it was initially published, Interaction was, like everything
Josef Albers did, a brave experiment, and like all forays into the unprecedented, it
translated_text: 纺织品、室内设计以及各个技术层级的图形媒介中被使用和被感知的方式。然而我们不应忘记，《相互作用》最初出版时，正如约瑟夫·阿尔伯斯所做的一切一样，是一次勇敢的实验；而如同所有对于前所未有之事的探索，它

source_text: was the subject of controversy.
translated_text: 也曾成为争议的对象。

source_text: Even if for the most part Interaction was highly praised, occasionally the response
translated_text: 即便《相互作用》在很大程度上受到高度赞扬，偶尔也会出现

source_text:
was far from laudatory. Writers vary in their responses to negative criticism-some
saying it is fine, since all that counts is the amount of coverage, others feeling
stung. Josef Albers, who saw himself as something of a martyr to modernism,
both regretted the attacks and was intrigued by them. Part of the fascination
of being blasted was that it confirmed that he had really startled people and taken
them beyond their normal comfort zone. Ever since he had left a world where art was
practiced in an acceptable, academic way-in the academies of Berlin and Munich,
and in the public education system in which he taught in his native Westphalia-and
gone to the Bauhaus, he had known what it was to inspire such controversial response.
translated_text: 远非褒奖的回应。作家们对负面批评的反应各不相同——有人说这无妨，因为唯一重要的是报道量；也有人感到刺痛。约瑟夫·阿尔伯斯把自己看作某种现代主义的殉道者，他既对这些攻击感到遗憾，又为之着迷。遭到猛烈抨击的迷人之处，部分在于它证实了他确实使人们大为震动，并把他们带出了通常的舒适地带。自从他离开那个以可接受的、学院式方式从事艺术的世界——柏林和慕尼黑的学院，以及他在故乡威斯特法伦任教的公共教育体系——转而前往包豪斯以来，他便已经知道激发这种争议性反应意味着什么。

source_text:
Bauhaus modernism may now be in the pantheon of acceptability, but back then it
startled and displeased the larger audience. The same was true of Black Mountain
College, where Albers went after 1933, when the Bauhaus closed, and where he
remained for sixteen years; today that pioneering institution is worshiped, but at
the time a lot of what was created there was viewed as a form of heresy. Later,
in 1950, when Albers began his Homages to the Square, he was mocked. Twenty
years after that, when he was the first living artist given a solo retrospective at
The Metropolitan Museum of Art, the work that people like Clement Greenberg
translated_text: 包豪斯现代主义如今或许已进入可接受性的万神殿，但在当时，它使更广大的受众震惊并不悦。黑山学院也是如此：1933年包豪斯关闭后，阿尔伯斯前往那里，并在那里停留了十六年；今天，这所开创性机构备受崇敬，但在当时，那里创造的许多东西被视为一种异端。后来，1950年，当阿尔伯斯开始创作《向方形致敬》时，他遭到了嘲笑。二十年后，当他成为第一位在大都会艺术博物馆获得个人回顾展的在世艺术家时，那些曾被克莱门特·格林伯格等人

source_text:
had lambasted was finally recognized for its ingenuity, integrity, and subsuming
beauty. Now that half a century has passed it has achieved the status, however
dubious, of being a blue chip financial commodity, but at the start it was, like any
statement by a messiah, criticized vociferously.
translated_text: 猛烈抨击的作品，终于因其机巧、完整性和包容一切的美而得到承认。半个世纪过去后的今天，它已经获得了某种地位，尽管可疑，即成为蓝筹金融商品；但在起初，它像任何弥赛亚的宣言一样，遭到了激烈批评。

source_text: ix
translated_text: ix

source_text:
When Yale University Press courageously, and with all of the superb standards
required by as exacting an artist as Albers, brought out Interaction of Colorin 1963,
the publication generally had an easier time than most of the artist's ventures. This
was equally true when the paperback version came out in 1971. But there was the
occasional diatribe. And Albers, proud as he was of the sales and all the enthusiasm
for the book, of the applause worldwide, was fascinated at being a lightning rod for
dissent. The octogenarian clipped the few bad reviews that appeared along with
dozens of favorable ones and tried to find out more about their authors. The voices
of "nay" appeared in obscure publications, but they still counted. One of the reasons
the artist was so interested was that the things for which the critics attacked the books
were exactly the elements that excited him the most, because they recommended such
a radical departure from traditional, hidebound ways of seeing.
translated_text: 1963年，耶鲁大学出版社以勇气，并以阿尔伯斯这样一位苛求的艺术家所要求的一切卓越标准，推出《色彩的相互作用》时，该书的出版总体上比这位艺术家的多数事业更为顺利。1971年平装本问世时亦是如此。但偶尔也会有长篇抨击。阿尔伯斯固然为该书的销量、所有热情反响以及全世界的掌声感到自豪，却也为自己成为异议的避雷针而着迷。这位八旬老人剪下了少数几篇差评，与几十篇好评放在一起，并试图进一步了解它们的作者。“反对”的声音出现在一些不知名的刊物上，但它们仍然算数。这位艺术家如此感兴趣的原因之一，是批评者攻击这些书的方面，恰恰正是最令他兴奋的元素，因为它们倡导如此激进地背离传统而僵化的观看方式。

source_text:
Arthur Carp was the author of an attack in the magazine Leonardo. To present
the flaws, Carp wrote that Albers considered "good teaching ... 'more a matter
of right questions than ... of right answers.' He deprecates 'self-expression,' as
opposed to 'a basic step-by-step learning.' ... Students are urged to use disliked
colors in the hope they may overcome their prejudices." Carp used these points to
demonstrate that "one doubts if Albers is really being helpful" and to justify the
statement "Would that he were less of a dilettante (pejorative connotation)!"
translated_text: 阿瑟·卡普是在《莱昂纳多》杂志上发表一篇攻击文章的作者。为了指出缺陷，卡普写道，阿尔伯斯认为“好的教学……‘与其说是正确答案的问题，不如说是正确提问的问题。’他贬低‘自我表达’，而推崇‘一种循序渐进的基础学习。’……学生被鼓励使用不喜欢的颜色，希望他们能够克服自己的偏见。”卡普用这些观点来证明“人们怀疑阿尔伯斯是否真的有所助益”，并为“但愿他少一些业余爱好者气质（贬义）！”这一说法辩护。

source_text:
Everything that Carp attacked, of course, was what Albers believed in and what
others applauded. As Howard Sayre Weaver wrote in a review that appeared in
translated_text: 当然，卡普所攻击的一切，正是阿尔伯斯所相信的，也是其他人所赞赏的。正如霍华德·塞尔·韦弗在一篇发表于

source_text:
1963 following publication of the first edition, Interaction of Color was a "grand
passport to perception." It assumed that glorious role because it was, "essentially, a
process: a unique means of learning and teaching and experiencing."
translated_text: 1963年第一版出版后的评论中所写，《色彩的相互作用》是一张“通往感知的宏伟通行证”。它之所以承担起这一光辉角色，是因为它“本质上是一种过程：一种独特的学习、教学和体验方式”。

source_text: Weaver referred to Albers's fondness for the words of John Ruskin: "Hundreds of
translated_text: 韦弗提到阿尔伯斯喜爱约翰·拉斯金的这句话：“数百人

source_text:
people can talk, for one who can think. But thousands of people can think, for
one who can see." Most people, sooner or later, have recognized the miraculous
way in which Interaction of Color facilitates such seeing. In the 1963 Architectural
Forum, a design teacher at Cooper Union was among those prescient enough to
write, "Interaction of Color is the most comprehensive and intelligent, as well as the
handsomest, book we yet have on this subject. It is an indispensable volume for
the artist, architect, or teacher who finds a greater challenge in discovery than
in a 'safe' color system." That same year, Dore Ashton, reviewing the book in
translated_text: 会说话，才有一个会思考的人。但数千人会思考，才有一个会看的人。”大多数人迟早都会认识到，《色彩互动》以近乎神奇的方式促成了这种观看。在1963年的《建筑论坛》上，库珀联盟学院的一位设计教师便是那些颇具先见之明的人之一，他写道：“《色彩互动》是迄今为止我们在这一主题上所拥有的最全面、最睿智，同时也是最美观的一本书。对于那些在发现中比在某种‘安全’的色彩体系中看到更大挑战的艺术家、建筑师或教师来说，这是一本不可或缺的著作。”同年，多尔·阿什顿在

source_text:
Studio, was perceptive enough to recognize that Albers was the opposite of the
pedagogue Carp accused him of being; rather, his achievement justified his
comment that "teaching is not a matter of method but of heart." The year after the
paperback came out, the poet Mark Strand, in Saturday Review, saw Josef Albers's
work as demonstrating that "when color challenges the safe, enclosing geometrical
translated_text: 《工作室》上评论此书时，敏锐地认识到阿尔伯斯恰恰不是卡普所指责的那种教育者；相反，他的成就证明了他那句话的正当性：“教学不是方法的问题，而是心的问题。”平装本问世后的第二年，诗人马克·斯特兰德在《星期六评论》上认为，约瑟夫·阿尔伯斯的作品表明，“当色彩挑战画面表面那种安全的、封闭性的几何

source_text: X
translated_text: X

source_text:
properties of the pictorial surface, as it is meant to, it does so with a slowness and
delicacy that are disarming and a beauty that is exhilarating."
translated_text: 属性时，正如它本应如此，它是以一种令人卸下防备的缓慢与细腻，以及一种令人振奋的美来做到这一点的。”

source_text:
What one person disdained, another saw as groundbreaking. Albers's approach
was revolutionary, putting experimentation at the fore. It disputed traditional
notions of taste. It sought to engage rather than merely inform.
translated_text: 一个人所轻蔑的东西，另一个人却视为开创性的事物。阿尔伯斯的方法是革命性的，它把实验置于最前沿。它质疑传统的趣味观念。它力求使人参与其中，而不仅仅是告知。

source_text:
As a keen observer of the human comedy, Albers was particularly aware that
sometimes his detractors were well-known figures, and his champions obscure
ones. Donald Judd, in ARTS Magazine in 1963, called Interaction o/Color"primarily
pedagogical." Judd went on with a mixture of moderate, pseudo-Hemingwayesque
adulation-"The book makes, to put it simply, one unqualified point, that color
is important in art. It does this very well."-and bizarre, incomprehensible
disparagement: "The Interaction of Color is the best that can be done. It is just that
it has all the Biblical possibilities, since it is clear and has limits, of anatomy or
of the other subjects whose presence and perfection are supposed to define art.
The book should be used but not that way." Albers would never know that Judd
would, two decades later, following the older artist's death, rescind these words
and make pilgrimages to Albers's studio, feeling that he had not done justice to
what Interaction was all about and regretting his youthful arrogance. In any event,
translated_text: 作为人间喜剧的敏锐观察者，阿尔伯斯尤其清楚，有时批评他的是知名人物，而支持他的却是无名之辈。唐纳德·贾德于1963年在《艺术杂志》上称《色彩互动》“主要是教学性的”。贾德接着以一种温和的、伪海明威式的赞美写道：“简单地说，这本书提出了一个毫无保留的观点，即色彩在艺术中很重要。它把这一点做得非常好。”同时又作出一种古怪而令人费解的贬抑：“《色彩互动》已经是所能做到的最好了。只是由于它清晰且有限，它具有解剖学或其他那些被认为其存在与完善足以界定艺术的学科的一切《圣经》式可能性。应当使用这本书，但不应当那样使用。”阿尔伯斯永远不会知道，二十年后，在这位年长艺术家去世之后，贾德会收回这些话，并前往阿尔伯斯的工作室朝圣，觉得自己没有公正对待《互动》的真正意义，并为自己年轻时的傲慢感到后悔。无论如何，

source_text:
taking it all in stride, Albers was certainly pleased that an unknown academic at the
University of Nevada in Las Vegas had been among those to get the main point, in
spades, of Interaction: "In an age in which increased human sensibility has become such
an obvious need in all areas of human involvement, color sensitivity and awareness can
constitute a major weapon against forces of insensitivity and brutalization."
translated_text: 阿尔伯斯泰然处之；他当然会感到欣慰的是，内华达大学拉斯维加斯分校一位名不见经传的学者，已经是那些充分领会《互动》要点的人之一：“在一个人类敏感性在所有人类参与领域中显然已成为如此迫切需要的时代，色彩敏感性与意识可以构成一件对抗麻木与野蛮化力量的重要武器。”

source_text:
This was the point. The quality of heart, the impact on all of human life, was what
Josef Albers sought in his approach. This above all is the reason that we are so
translated_text: 这正是关键所在。心的品质，对整个人类生活的影响，正是约瑟夫·阿尔伯斯在其方法中所追求的。最重要的是，正因为如此，我们才如此

source_text:
pleased that Yale University Press, Josef Albers's partner through thick and thin
for five decades, has remained in that role as splendidly as ever. Supportive of
translated_text: 欣慰于耶鲁大学出版社作为约瑟夫·阿尔伯斯五十年来同甘共苦的伙伴，依然一如既往地出色扮演着这一角色。它在他生前创作之际支持他，

source_text:
the artist's legacy as it was of him during his lifetime when he was in the act of
creating, Yale has shown a wonderful and consistent understanding of the brazen,
self-generating newness of the artist's approach. Thanks to that fine relationship,
Albers's marvelous, unsettling revelations-unsettling to some, exhilarating to
others-are again flourishing in this current incarnation of Interaction of Color. With
its additional plates and refinement of other details, this new, fiftieth-anniversary
volume, which effectively updates what is now a "classic," allows Albers's courageous
invitation to experimentation, openness, and intellectual and personal expansion to
thrive. It invites readers to thrive as well-exactly as Josef Albers would have liked.
translated_text: 也同样支持这位艺术家的遗产；耶鲁对这位艺术家方法中那种大胆的、自我生成的新颖性，表现出一种出色而始终如一的理解。得益于这种良好的关系，阿尔伯斯那些奇妙而令人不安的启示——对某些人而言令人不安，对另一些人而言令人振奋——如今又在《色彩互动》当前这一化身中蓬勃生长。凭借新增的图版和其他细节的完善，这部新的五十周年纪念版有效地更新了如今已成为“经典”的作品，使阿尔伯斯那份勇敢的邀请——邀请人们走向实验、开放，以及智识与个人的拓展——得以兴盛。它也邀请读者一同兴盛——这正是约瑟夫·阿尔伯斯所乐见的。

source_text: Nicholas Fox Weber
translated_text: 尼古拉斯·福克斯·韦伯

source_text: xi
translated_text: xi

source_text: Interaction of Color
translated_text: 色彩互动

source_text: Introduction
translated_text: 导言

source_text:
The book "Interaction of Color" is a record of an experimental way of
studying color and of teaching color.
translated_text: 《色彩互动》一书，是以实验方式研究色彩和教授色彩的一份记录。

source_text:
In visual perception a color is almost never seen as it really is
-as it physically is.
This fact makes color the most relative medium in art.
translated_text:
在视觉感知中，一种色彩几乎从不会被看成它真正的样子——也就是它在物理上的样子。
这一事实使色彩成为艺术中最具相对性的媒介。

source_text:
In order to use color effectively it is necessary to recognize
that color deceives continually.
To this end, the beginning is not a study of color systems.
translated_text:
为了有效地使用色彩，有必要认识到：色彩始终在欺骗。
为此，起点并不是研究色彩体系。

source_text:
First, it should be learned that one and the same color evokes
innumerable readings.
Instead of mechanically applying or merely implying laws and rules
of color harmony, distinct color effects are produced
-through recognition of the interaction of color-
translated_text:
首先，应当学会，同一种色彩会引发无数种解读。
不是机械地应用或仅仅暗示色彩和谐的法则与规则，而是通过认识色彩的互动，产生明确的色彩效果——

source_text: by making, for instance,
translated_text: 例如，通过使

source_text: 2 very different colors look alike, or nearly alike.
translated_text: 两种截然不同的色彩看起来相同，或几乎相同。

source_text:
The aim of such study is to develop- through experience
-by trial and error-an eye for color.
This means, specifically, seeing color action
as well as feeling color relatedness.
translated_text:
这种研究的目的，是通过经验——通过反复试错——培养对色彩的眼力。
具体而言，这意味着既要看见色彩的作用，也要感受色彩之间的关联。

source_text: As a general training it means development of observation and articulation.
translated_text: 作为一种一般训练，它意味着观察力与表达能力的发展。

source_text:
This book, therefore, does not follow an academic conception
of "theory and practice."
It reverses this order and places practice before theory,
which, after all, is the conclusion of practice.
translated_text:
因此，本书并不遵循“理论与实践”的学院式观念。
它颠倒了这一顺序，把实践置于理论之前；毕竟，理论是实践的结论。

source_text:
Also, the book does not begin with optics and physiology of visual perception,
nor with any presentation of the physics of light and wave length.
translated_text: 此外，本书并不以视觉感知的光学和生理学开篇，也不从任何关于光与波长物理学的阐述开始。

source_text: Just as the knowledge of acoustics does not make one musical
translated_text: 正如声学知识并不能使人具有音乐性

source_text:
-neither on the productive nor on the appreciative side-
so no color system by itself can develop one's sensitivity for color.
This is parallel to the recognition that no theory of composition by itself
leads to the production of music, or of art.
translated_text: ——无论是在创作方面还是在欣赏方面——同样，任何色彩体系本身也不能培养一个人对色彩的敏感性。这与这样一种认识相一致：任何构成理论本身都不会导向音乐或艺术的创作。

source_text:
Practical exercises demonstrate through color deception (illusion)
the relativity and instability of color.
And experience teaches that in visual perception there is a discrepancy
translated_text: 实践练习通过色彩欺骗（错觉）展示色彩的相对性和不稳定性。经验还表明，在视觉感知中存在一种差异

source_text: between physical fact and psychic effect.
translated_text: 存在于物理事实与心理效果之间。

source_text:
What counts here-first and last-is not so-called knowledge
of so-called facts, but vision-seeing.
Seeing here implies Schauen (as in Weltanschauung) and is coupled
with fantasy, with imagination.
translated_text: 在这里，从始至终，重要的不是所谓对所谓事实的知识，而是视觉——观看。这里的观看意味着 Schauen（如 Weltanschauung 中的 schauen），并与幻想、想象相联结。
这种探寻方式将从对色彩与色彩之间相互作用的视觉体认，通向对色彩与形状及位置的相互依存关系的认识；与数量的关系（数量分别衡量多少、延展和/或数目，包括重复出现）；与质量的关系（光的强度和/或色相）；以及与表述的关系（通过分离或连接边界）。

source_text:
The table of contents shows the order
in which exercises usually lead our investigation.
translated_text: 目录显示了练习通常引导我们展开探究的顺序。

source_text:
Each exercise is explained and illustrated-
not to give a specific answer,
but to suggest a way of study.
translated_text: 每项练习都配有说明和图示——不是为了给出某个特定答案，而是为了提示一种研究方式。

source_text: I Color recollection-visual memory
translated_text: I 色彩回忆——视觉记忆

source_text:
If one says "Red" ( the name of a color)
and there are 50 people listening,
translated_text: 如果有人说“红”（一种颜色的名称），并且有 50 个人在听，

source_text:
it can be expected that there will be 50 reds in their minds.
And one can be sure that all these reds will be very different.
translated_text: 可以预期，他们心中会有 50 种红。并且可以肯定，所有这些红都会彼此大不相同。

source_text:
Even when a certain color is specified which all listeners have seen
innumerable times-such as the red of the Coca-Cola signs which is
the same red all over the country-they will still think of
many different reds.
translated_text: 即使指定某种所有听者都见过无数次的特定颜色——例如可口可乐标志的红色，这种红色在全国各地都是同一种红——他们仍会想到许多不同的红。

source_text:
Even if all the listeners have hundreds of reds in front of them
from which to choose the Coca-Cola red, they will again select
quite different colors. And no one can be sure that he has found
translated_text: 即使所有听者面前都有数百种红可供选择，让他们从中选出可口可乐的红色，他们也会再次选出相当不同的颜色。并且没有人能够确信自己找到了

source_text: the precise red shade.
translated_text: 那个精确的红色色调。

source_text:
And even
if that round red Coca-Cola sign with the white name in the middle
is actually shown so that everyone focuses on the same red,
each will receive the same projection on his retina,
but no one can be sure whether each has the same perception.
translated_text: 而即使那个中间有白色名称的圆形红色可口可乐标志被实际展示出来，使每个人都注视同一种红，每个人的视网膜上都会接收到同样的投射，但没有人能够确信每个人是否具有同样的感知。

source_text:
When we consider further the associations and reactions
which are experienced in connection with the color and the name,
probably everyone will diverge again in many different directions.
translated_text: 当我们进一步考虑与这种颜色和名称相关联的联想与反应时，很可能每个人又会朝许多不同方向分化开来。

source_text: What does this show?
translated_text: 这说明了什么？

source_text:
First, it is hard, if not impossible, to remember distinct colors.
This underscores the important fact that the visual memory is very poor
in comparison with our auditory memory. Often the latter is able
to repeat a melody heard only once or twice.
translated_text: 第一，记住明确的颜色是困难的，即便不是不可能的。这突出说明了一个重要事实：与我们的听觉记忆相比，视觉记忆非常薄弱。后者往往能够复现只听过一两次的旋律。

source_text:
Second, the nomenclature of color is most inadequate.
Though there are innumerable colors-shades and tones-
in daily vocabulary, there are only about 30 color names.
translated_text: 第二，色彩的命名法极不充分。尽管存在无数颜色——深浅与色调——在日常词汇中，颜色名称却只有大约 30 个。

source_text: II Color reading and contexture
translated_text: II 色彩阅读与脉络构成

source_text:
The concept that "the simpler the form of a letter the simpler its reading"
was an obsession of beginning constructivism. It became something
like a dogma, and is still followed by "modernistic" typographers.
translated_text: “字母的形式越简单，其阅读就越简单”这一观念，是早期构成主义的一种执念。它变成了近乎教条的东西，并且仍为“现代主义”字体设计师所遵循。

source_text:
This notion has proved to be wrong, because in reading we do not read
letters but words, words as a whole, as a "word picture."
This was discovered in psychology, particularly in Gestalt psychology.
Ophthalmology has disclosed that the more the letters are differentiated
from each other, the easier is the reading.
translated_text: 这一观念已被证明是错误的，因为在阅读时，我们读的不是字母，而是词，是作为整体的词，是作为“词的图像”的词。这一点是心理学，尤其是格式塔心理学所发现的。眼科学已经揭示，字母彼此之间区分得越明显，阅读就越容易。

source_text:
Without going into comparisons and details, it should be realized that words
consisting of only capital letters present the most difficult reading-
because of their equal height, equal volume, and, with most, their equal width.
When comparing serif letters with sans-serif, the latter provide an uneasy reading.
The fashionable preference for sans-serif in text shows neither historical
translated_text: 不作比较和细节展开也应认识到，仅由大写字母组成的词最难阅读——因为它们高度相同、体量相同，而且多数情况下宽度也相同。把衬线字体与无衬线字体相比较，后者会造成不舒适的阅读。文本中对无衬线字体的时髦偏好既不显示历史

source_text: nor practical competence.
translated_text: 能力，也不显示实践能力。

source_text:
First, sans-serifs were designed as letters not for texts but for captions,
when pictorial reproductions were introduced with stone lithography.
Second, they produce poor "word pictures."
translated_text: 首先，无衬线字体最初并不是为正文而设计的字母，而是为说明文字而设计的，当时随着石版印刷术，图像复制被引入。其次，它们产生的“词的图像”很差。

source_text:
INTERACTION OF COLOR
Interaction of Color
translated_text:
色彩的相互作用
色彩的相互作用

source_text:
INTERACTION OF COLOR
Interaction of Color
translated_text:
色彩的相互作用
色彩的相互作用

source_text: This illustrates that clear reading depends upon the recognition of context.
translated_text: 这说明，清晰阅读取决于对语境的识别。

source_text: In musical compositions,
translated_text: 在音乐作品中，

source_text:
so long as we hear merely single tones, we do not hear music.
Hearing music depends on the recognition of the in-between of the tones,
of their placing and of their spacing.
translated_text: 只要我们听到的仅仅是单个音，我们就没有听到音乐。听见音乐取决于对音与音之间的关系、对它们的位置和间隔的识别。

source_text:
In writing, a knowledge of spelling has nothing to do with an understanding
of poetry.
translated_text: 在写作中，拼写知识与理解诗歌毫无关系。

source_text:
Equally, a factual identification of colors within a given painting
has nothing to do with a sensitive seeing
nor with an understanding of the color action within the painting.
translated_text: 同样，对一幅既定绘画中的色彩作事实性的辨认，与敏锐的观看毫无关系，也与理解绘画中的色彩作用毫无关系。

source_text:
Our study of color differs fundamentally from a study which anatomically
dissects colorants (pigments) and physical qualities (wave length).
translated_text: 我们对色彩的研究，从根本上不同于那种对着色剂（颜料）和物理性质（波长）作解剖式分析的研究。

source_text:
Our concern is the interaction of color; that is, seeing
what happens between colors.
translated_text: 我们关注的是色彩的相互作用；也就是说，观看色彩之间发生了什么。

source_text:
We are able to hear a single tone.
But we almost never (that is, without special devices) see a single color
unconnected and unrelated to other colors.
Colors present themselves in continuous flux, constantly related to
changing neighbors and changing conditions.
translated_text: 我们能够听到一个单音。但我们几乎从来不会（也就是说，在没有特殊装置的情况下）看见一种与其他色彩不相连、无关系的单一色彩。色彩是在连续流变中呈现自身的，始终与变化中的邻近色和变化中的条件相关联。

source_text:
As a consequence, this proves for the reading of color
what Kandinsky often demanded for the reading of art:
what counts is not the what but the how.
translated_text: 因此，这为色彩的阅读证明了康定斯基常常要求于艺术阅读的东西：重要的不是“什么”，而是“如何”。

source_text:
Why color paper-
instead of pigment and paint
translated_text:
为什么使用色纸——
而不是颜料和绘画颜料

source_text: III
translated_text: III

source_text:
When, more than 20 years ago, this systematic study of color was begun,
it occurred almost as a matter of course that the studies would be done
in color papers. At that same time there was some concern among teachers
that students might be reluctant to substitute paper for paint.
Since then, obviously, the attitude of students-and of teachers-
has changed.
translated_text: 20多年前，当这项系统的色彩研究开始时，几乎自然而然地想到，研究会用色纸来完成。与此同时，教师们有些担心，学生可能不愿意用纸来替代颜料。此后，显然，学生——以及教师——的态度已经改变。

source_text:
In our studies, color paper is preferred to paint
for several practical reasons. Paper provides innumerable colors
in a large range of shades and tints ready for immediate use.
Though a large collection is needed, it is not expensive to assemble
when one does not rely on large prepared paper sets
representing specific color systems, such as the Munsell or Ostwald Systems
translated_text: 在我们的研究中，出于若干实际原因，色纸优于绘画颜料。纸张提供了无数可立即使用的色彩，具有范围广泛的深浅和色调。虽然需要大量收集，但只要不依赖那些代表特定色彩系统的大型预制纸张套装，如孟塞尔或奥斯特瓦尔德系统，收集起来并不昂贵

source_text: (the least desirable are "tuned" sets, claiming to be failure-proof).
translated_text: （最不可取的是那些“调谐”套装，它们声称不会出错）。

source_text:
Sources easily accessible for many kinds of color paper are waste strips
found at printers and bookbinders; collections of samples of packing papers,
of wrapping and bag papers, of cover and decoration papers. Also, instead
of full sheets of paper, just cutouts from magazines, from advertisements
and illustrations, from posters, wallpapers, paint samples,
and from catalogues with color reproductions of various materials will do.
Often a collective search for papers and a subsequent exchange of them
among class members will provide a rich but inexpensive color paper "palette."
translated_text: 许多种色纸都可以从容易获得的来源取得：印刷厂和装订厂的废纸条；包装纸、包裹纸和纸袋纸、封面纸和装饰纸的样品集。此外，不必使用整张纸，只需从杂志、广告和插图、海报、墙纸、涂料样本，以及带有各种材料彩色复制图的目录中剪下来的剪片也可以。通常，集体寻找纸张，并随后在班级成员之间交换，会提供一个丰富而廉价的色纸“调色板”。

source_text:
What are the advantages of working with color paper?
First, color paper avoids unnecessary mixing of paints, which is often difficult,
time-consuming, and tiring. This is true not merely for beginners alone.
translated_text: 使用色纸工作的优点是什么？首先，色纸避免了不必要的调配绘画颜料，而这往往困难、费时且令人疲惫。这不仅仅对初学者如此。

source_text:
Second, by not exposing the student to discouraging failures of mixing
and imperfect matching of spoiled paints and papers, we not only save
time and material, but, more important, gain a continued active interest.
translated_text: 第二，由于不让学生遭遇调配失败以及损坏的颜料和纸张无法完美匹配所带来的挫败，我们不仅节省了时间和材料，更重要的是，获得了持续的积极兴趣。

source_text:
Third, color paper permits a repeated use of precisely the same color
without the slightest change in tone, light, or surface quality. It permits
repetition without disturbing changes caused by varying application of paint
(thinner or thicker-even or uneven); without traces of hand or tool
resulting in varying density and intensity.
translated_text: 第三，彩色纸可以反复使用完全相同的颜色，而在色调、明度或表面质感上没有丝毫变化。它允许重复，而不会出现因颜料涂布方式不同（较薄或较厚——均匀或不均匀）所造成的令人分心的变化；也不会留下手或工具的痕迹，从而导致密度和强度的差异。

source_text: Fourth, working with color paper rarely demands more equipment than paste
translated_text: 第四，使用彩色纸很少需要比糨糊更多的设备

source_text:
(heavy rubber cement is best), and a single-edged razor blade instead of
scissors. This eliminates tools and equipment for handling paints, and therefore
is easier, cheaper, and more orderly.
translated_text: （厚质橡胶胶水最佳），以及一片单刃剃刀刀片，而不是剪刀。这省去了处理颜料所需的工具和设备，因此更容易、更便宜，也更有条理。

source_text:
Fifth, color paper also protects us from undesired and unnecessary addition
of so-called texture (such as brush marks and strokes, incalculable changes
from wet to dry, or heavy and loose covering, hard and soft boundaries, etc.)
which too often only hides poor color conception or application, or, worse,
an insensitive color handling.
translated_text: 第五，彩色纸还使我们免于不希望且不必要地添加所谓肌理（如笔痕和笔触、由湿到干的不可估量的变化，或厚重而松散的覆盖、硬边界和软边界等）；这些肌理往往只是掩盖了拙劣的色彩构想或运用，甚至更糟，是对色彩不敏感的处理。

source_text:
There is another valuable advantage in working with color papers
instead of with paints: in solving our problems again and again
we must find just the right color which demonstrates a desired effect.
We can choose from a large collection of tones, displayed in front of us,
and can thus constantly compare neighboring and contrasting colors.
This offers a training which no palette can provide.
translated_text: 使用彩色纸而不是颜料，还有另一个宝贵的优点：在一次又一次解决我们的问题时，我们必须找到恰好能够显示某种预期效果的颜色。我们可以从摆在眼前的大量色调中选择，因而能够不断比较相邻色和对比色。这提供了一种任何调色板都无法给予的训练。

source_text: A color has many faces-
translated_text: 一种颜色有许多面貌——

source_text: the relativity of color
translated_text: 色彩的相对性

source_text: IV
translated_text: IV

source_text: Imagine in front of us 3 pots containing water, from left to right:
translated_text: 想象我们面前有3只盛水的容器，从左到右依次是：

source_text:
WARM
LUKEWARM
COLD
translated_text:
温热
微温
冷

source_text:
When the hands are dipped first into the outer containers,
one feels-experiences-perceives-2 different temperatures:
translated_text: 当双手先浸入两侧的容器时，人会感觉到——体验到——感知到——2种不同的温度：

source_text:
Herewith one experiences
a discrepancy between physical fact and psychic effect called,
in this case, a haptic illusion-haptic as related to the sense of
touch-the haptic sense.
translated_text:
由此，人体验到
物理事实与心理效果之间的一种差异；
在这种情况下，它被称为触觉错觉——触觉是指与
触摸感相关的——触觉感。

source_text:
In much the same way as haptic sensations deceive us, so
optical illusions deceive. They lead us to "see" and to "read"
other colors than those with which we are confronted physically.
translated_text:
触觉感觉欺骗我们的方式，与此十分相似，
视觉错觉也会欺骗我们。它们使我们“看见”并“读出”
不同于我们在物理上所面对的那些颜色。

source_text:
To begin the study of how color deceives and how to make use of this,
the first exercise is
to make one and the same color look different.
translated_text:
要开始研究色彩如何欺骗，以及如何利用这种欺骗，
第一个练习是
使同一种颜色看起来不同。

source_text: On the blackboard and in our notebooks we write:
translated_text: 在黑板上和我们的笔记本中，我们写道：

source_text: Color is the most relative medium in art.
translated_text: 色彩是艺术中最具相对性的媒介。

source_text:
Challenging examples of very surprising color changes are shown.
Then the class is invited to produce similar effects
but is not given reasons or favorable conditions.
It starts, therefore, on a trial-and-error basis.
translated_text:
展示了一些极具挑战性的例子，呈现出十分令人惊讶的色彩变化。
随后请全班产生类似的效果，
但不提供理由或有利条件。
因此，课程以试错为基础开始。

source_text: Thus, continuing comparison-observation-"thinking in situations" -
translated_text: 这样，持续的比较—观察—“在情境中思考”——

source_text:
is promoted, making the class aware that discovery and invention
are the criteria of creativeness.
translated_text:
得到促进，使全班意识到，发现与发明
是创造性的标准。

source_text:
As a practical study we ask that 2 small rectangles of the same color
and the same size be placed on large grounds of very different color.
translated_text:
作为一项实践研究，我们要求将2个颜色相同、
大小相同的小矩形放置在颜色差异很大的大底面上。

source_text:
Soon, these first trials are collected and separated into groups
of more and less promise.
The class will become aware that change is a result of influence.
The influencing color is distinguished from the influenced color.
translated_text:
很快，这些最初的尝试被收集起来，并分成
较有希望和较少希望的几组。
全班将会意识到，变化是影响的结果。
施加影响的颜色与受影响的颜色被区分开来。

source_text:
It is discovered that certain colors are hard to change, and
that there are others more susceptible to change.
translated_text:
人们发现，某些颜色难以改变，
而另一些颜色则更容易受到改变。

source_text:
We try to find those colors which are more inclined to exert influence
and to distinguish them from those which will accept influence.
translated_text:
我们试图找出那些更倾向于施加影响的颜色，
并将它们同那些会接受影响的颜色区分开来。

source_text:
A second class exhibition of more advanced results should clarify
that there are 2 kinds of changing influences working in 2 directions,
translated_text:
第二次课堂展览展示更为进阶的成果，应当阐明，
有2种改变性的影响在2个方向上起作用，

source_text:
light on the one side and hue on the other. And both occur simultaneously-
though in varying strength.
translated_text:
一方是明度，另一方是色相。而且二者同时发生——
尽管强度各不相同。

source_text:
Since 2 pieces of the same paper, therefore of the same color,
are to appear different-and, if possible, incredibly different-
we must compare them under equal conditions.
The only colors which are factually different are the large grounds,
translated_text:
既然2片同一种纸，因而是同一种颜色，
要显得不同——并且，如果可能的话，显得不可思议地不同——
我们就必须在相同条件下比较它们。
事实上唯一不同的颜色，是那些大底面，

source_text: though they are alike in size and shape.
translated_text: 尽管它们的大小和形状相同。

source_text:
Because of the laboratory character of these studies
there is no opportunity to decorate, to illustrate, to represent anything,
or to express something-or one's self.
translated_text:
由于这些研究具有实验室性质，
因此没有机会去装饰、去图解、去再现任何事物，
或去表达某种东西——或表达自我。

source_text:
Here, successful studies present a demonstration. Since they cannot be
misread or misunderstood, they prove understanding both
of the principle involved and of the materials to be manipulated.
translated_text:
在这里，成功的研究呈现的是一种示范。由于它们不会被
误读或误解，它们证明了对所涉及原则以及
对所要操作材料的理解。

source_text: (See plates 1v-1 and 1v-3.)
translated_text: （见图版1v-1和1v-3。）

source_text:
It should be clear that, with these exercises and all others to follow,
whether or not we arrive at a pleasant or harmonious color combination
is unimportant.
translated_text:
应当明确的是，对于这些练习以及随后所有其他练习，
我们是否得到一种令人愉悦或和谐的色彩组合，
并不重要。

Precision and clean execution are required for all finished studies.
To avoid destroying the desired effect, small pieces of paper

Arrangements such as the one shown below disguise the desired effect

为避免破坏所期望的效果，不应在小底面上
使用小纸片。

source_text:
If one is not able to distinguish the difference between a higher tone
and a lower tone, one probably should not make music.
translated_text: 如果一个人不能分辨较高音与较低音之间的差异，他大概就不该从事音乐。

source_text:
If a parallel conclusion were to be applied to color, almost everyone
would prove incompetent for its proper use. Very few are able to distinguish
higher and lower light intensity (usually called higher and lower value)
between different hues. This is true despite our daily reading of numerous
black-and-white pictures.
translated_text: 如果把一个类似的结论应用于色彩，几乎每个人都会被证明不能胜任对色彩的正确运用。很少有人能够在不同色相之间分辨较高与较低的光强度（通常称为较高与较低的明度值）。尽管我们每天阅读大量黑白图片，情况仍是如此。

source_text:
Since the discovery of photography and particularly since the development
ofphotomechanical reproduction processes, we are exposed-more and more
every day-to pictures from all over the world, the world seen and unseen,
visible and invisible.
translated_text: 自摄影术被发现以来，尤其自照相机械复制工艺发展以来，我们每天越来越多地接触到来自世界各地的图像，接触到可见与不可见的世界，见得到与见不到的世界。

source_text:
These pictures, which are predominantly "black and white,"
are printed in only I black on a white ground. Visually, however,
translated_text: 这些主要为“黑白”的图片，只是以一种黑色印在白色底面上。然而，在视觉上，

source_text:
these pictures consist of grey shades of the finest gradations
between the poles of black and white. These shades penetrate each other
in varying degrees.
translated_text: 这些图片由黑与白两极之间最细微层级的灰色调构成。这些色调以不同程度彼此渗透。

source_text:
With the tremendous increase in pictorial information
-through newspapers, magazines, books-we receive a training
in the reading of lighter and darker tones of grey as has never before
existed. With the growing interest in color photography and color reproduction,
a parallel training in the reading of lighter and darker color is on the way.
translated_text: 随着通过报纸、杂志、书籍获得的图像信息急剧增加，我们接受了一种前所未有的训练，即阅读较亮和较暗的灰色调。随着人们对彩色摄影和彩色复制兴趣的增长，阅读较亮和较暗色彩的相应训练也正在形成。

source_text:
However, it is still true that only a minority can distinguish
the lighter from the darker within close intervals
when obscured by contrasting hues or by different color intensities.
translated_text: 然而，事实仍然是：当受到对比色相或不同色彩强度的遮蔽时，只有少数人能够在相近的间隔内分辨较亮与较暗。

source_text:
In order to correct a prejudice common among painters and designers-
that they belong to that minority-
we have the students test themselves. We confront them
with several pairs of color, from which they are to select and to record
which color in a pair is the darker.
translated_text: 为了纠正画家和设计师中常见的一种偏见——即认为自己属于那少数人——我们让学生进行自我测试。我们把几组成对的颜色摆在他们面前，要求他们从每一对中选择并记录哪一种颜色较暗。

source_text:
The darker one, it is explained, is visually the heavier one, or the one containing
more black, or less white. It should be mentioned that the students
are encouraged to abstain from making a judgment in any case of doubt.
It may also demonstrate that not voting can have a positive meaning.
translated_text: 我们解释说，较暗的那一种在视觉上就是较重的那一种，或是含有更多黑色、或更少白色的那一种。应当说明的是，学生们被鼓励在任何有疑问的情况下不作判断。这也可以表明，不投票也可能具有积极意义。

source_text:
Though there have always been advanced painting students in the basic
color class, the result of this test has remained constant for a number
of years: 60% of the answers are wrong and only 40% are right,
not counting the undecided cases.
translated_text: 尽管基础色彩课中一直有高年级绘画学生，这项测试的结果多年来始终不变：不计未决的情况，60%的答案是错误的，只有40%是正确的。

source_text:
By this experience we are led to the next task: To find colors about
which we cannot say immediately which is the lighter or darker.
These colors are collected and pasted in pairs, and observed again
and again until their light-dark relationship is clearly recognized.
translated_text: 这一经验引向下一项任务：找出那些我们无法立即说出哪一个较亮或较暗的颜色。把这些颜色成对收集并粘贴起来，反复观察，直到清楚辨认出它们的明暗关系。

source_text:
In cases where a decision seems impossible, an after-image effect may be
helpful. 2 color sheets are put on top of each other
in this way:
translated_text: 在似乎无法作出判断的情况下，残像效果可能有所帮助。将2张彩色纸按如下方式叠放在一起：

source_text:
Focus longer than the eye wants to on the covering corner (B) of the
upper paper and then quickly remove this upper sheet. If area ( c)
now appears lighter than area (A), then the upper paper is the darker-
and vice versa. After this, repeat the experiment with the papers in
reverse order. Frequently only 1 of the 2 reversed comparisons
reveals the true relationship.
translated_text: 将目光停留在上方纸张起遮盖作用的一角（B）上，时间要比眼睛愿意停留的更久一些，然后迅速移开这张上方的纸。如果区域（c）此时显得比区域（A）更亮，那么上方的纸就是较暗的那一张，反之亦然。之后，将两张纸的顺序颠倒，重复这一实验。常常只有两次颠倒比较中的一次能揭示真实关系。

source_text:
The usual results (60% wrong) are disillusioning as well as revealing.
Voting for the wrong color often needs cover or compensation; also,
the disappointment of wrong answers encourages doubts.
The doubts often are directed, not against one's own judgment, but against
the competence of the teacher: are his answers the right ones?
translated_text: 通常的结果（60%错误）既令人失望，又具有启示性。投票选错颜色往往需要遮掩或补偿；同时，错误答案所带来的失望也会引发怀疑。这些怀疑常常并非指向自己的判断，而是指向教师的能力：他的答案是正确的吗？

source_text: As the test is to prove whether one has a trained eye or not,
translated_text: 由于这一测试是为了证明一个人是否具备训练有素的眼力，

source_text:
the pairs of color presented for discrimination are not easy to decipher.
Within the pairs there is no equal light intensity
translated_text: 所呈现出来供辨别的成对颜色并不容易破译。在这些成对颜色之中，并不存在相等的光强度，

source_text:
because the conclusive question to be expected from a class is:
are there equal light values within these couples?
The answer is No.
translated_text: 因为可以预期班上会提出的决定性问题是：这些成对颜色中是否存在相等的明度值？答案是否定的。

source_text: Another unavoidable question is: will a photograph of these colors
translated_text: 另一个不可避免的问题是：这些颜色的照片是否会

source_text:
reveal their true relationship and thus give the final proof?
The answer again is No.
translated_text: 揭示它们的真实关系，从而给出最终证明？答案同样是否定的。

source_text:
This answer will remain true for black-and-white
as well as color photographs, because the sensitivity
and consequently the registration of the retina of an eye is different
from the sensitivity and registration of a photographic film.
translated_text: 无论是黑白照片还是彩色照片，这一答案都依然成立，因为眼睛视网膜的敏感度以及由此产生的记录方式，不同于摄影胶片的敏感度和记录方式。

source_text:
Normally, black-and-white photography registers all lights lighter
and all darks darker than the more adjustable eye perceives them.
The eye also distinguishes better the so-called middle greys,
which in photography often are flattened if not lost.
translated_text: 通常，黑白摄影会把所有亮部记录得比适应性更强的眼睛所感知到的更亮，把所有暗部记录得更暗。眼睛还更善于区分所谓的中间灰，而这些中间灰在摄影中往往即使没有消失，也会被压平。

source_text:
As an example we showed our class 2 different reproductions of the
same Ensor painting, "Masks Confronting Death," of 1888. The first
appeared in the catalogue of an Ensor exhibition, the other in a
newspaper report on the same exhibition.
translated_text: 作为例子，我们向班上的学生展示了同一幅恩索尔1888年绘画《面具对峙死亡》的两种不同复制品。第一种出现在一次恩索尔展览的目录中，另一种出现在关于同一展览的报纸报道中。

source_text:
The first, the larger and more official reproduction, in very fine screen
on coated paper, presumably would be considered more representative than
the second, smaller reproduction in a coarser screen and on the
cheapest paper.
translated_text: 第一种复制品较大，也更具官方性质，采用非常精细的网屏，印在铜版纸上，大概会被认为比第二种更具代表性；第二种复制品较小，网屏较粗，且印在最廉价的纸张上。

source_text: But the latter was not only much more correct in its whole tonality;
translated_text: 但后者不仅在整体色调上准确得多；

source_text: it also showed clearly 1 more mask, face, or head which the more
translated_text: 它还清楚地显示出又一个面具、面孔或头部，而那个更

source_text:
expensive, so-called high-key reproduction blotted out entirely-a small
but complete frontal face, lighter than all the others and separated
from them, near the left picture edge.
translated_text: 昂贵的、所谓高调复制品则把它完全抹去了：那是一张小而完整的正面脸，位于画面左边缘附近，比所有其他面孔都更亮，并且与它们分离。

source_text: This shows what a higher key in light can lose in photography.
translated_text: 这表明，在摄影中，较高的亮调会失去什么。

source_text:
The greatest advantage the eye has over photography
is its scotopic seeing in addition to its photopic seeing.
The former means, briefly, the retinal adjustment to lower light conditions.
translated_text: 眼睛相对于摄影的最大优势，在于它除了明视觉之外还具有暗视觉。简而言之，后者指的是视网膜对较低光照条件的适应。

source_text:
Color photography deviates still more from eye vision
than black-and-white photography. Blue and red are overemphasized
to such an extent that their brightness is exaggerated.
Though this may flatter public taste, the result is a loss
translated_text: 彩色摄影比黑白摄影更偏离眼睛的视觉。蓝色和红色被过分强调，以至于它们的亮度被夸大。虽然这可能迎合公众趣味，其结果却是在更精细的细微差别和微妙关系上的损失。

source_text:
in finer nuances and in delicate relationships.
Whites rarely appear white but usually look greenish.
This makes color slides of Mondrian paintings unbearable.
translated_text: 白色很少显得是白色，通常看起来带绿色。这使得蒙德里安绘画的彩色幻灯片令人难以忍受。

source_text: Gradation studies-new presentations
translated_text: 渐变研究——新的呈现

source_text: With the experience that often we are unsure and thus unable
translated_text: 由于我们常常不确定，因而无法

source_text:
to distinguish between lighter and darker in color, it appears appropriate, even
necessary, to develop a more discriminating sensitivity. To this end,
translated_text: 在颜色中辨别较亮与较暗，有鉴于此，发展一种更具辨别力的敏感性显得恰当，甚至是必要的。为此，

source_text:
we study gradation by producing so-called grey steps, grey scales,
grey ladders. These demonstrate a gradual stepping up or down between
translated_text: 我们通过制作所谓的灰阶、灰度尺、灰梯来研究渐变。这些展示了在

source_text: white and black, between lighter and darker.
translated_text: 白与黑之间、较亮与较暗之间逐级上升或下降的过程。

source_text:
For such exercises, we first collect as many greys in paper as possible,
and preferably independent of commercial grey sets, which usually offer
translated_text:
在这类练习中，我们首先尽可能多地收集纸上的灰色，
并且最好不依赖商业灰色套装，因为它们通常提供

source_text:
a too limited choice, or, worse, unequal steps. Rich sources for
many paper greys are black-and-white reproductions from popular magazines.
translated_text:
过于有限的选择，或者更糟的是，阶差并不均等。获取
大量纸上灰色的丰富来源，是通俗杂志中的黑白复制图像。

source_text: Selecting from them smaller and larger areas of as many greys as possible,
translated_text: 从其中选取尽可能多的灰色的较小和较大区域，

source_text:
we will be taught first that photography registers and measures light and
dark differently from our eyes. That it turns darks darker and lights
lighter means, besides a generalization toward the polar contrasts,
a loss of the visually more interesting middle greys. Thus, such
reproductions confront us with a dominance of very heavy and very light
greys, and a consequent scarcity of middle greys.
translated_text: 我们首先会认识到，摄影记录和测量明暗的方式不同于我们的眼睛。它把暗部变得更暗、把亮部变得更亮，这意味着，除了朝向两极对比的一般化之外，还会丧失视觉上更有趣的中间灰。因此，这类复制图像让我们面对的是极重和极浅灰色的主导，以及由此造成的中间灰的稀缺。

source_text:
These cutouts are to be arranged in gradations as described. The softer
the steps appear, and the more equal the steps are, the more valuable
and convincing the study. As any lines or empty spaces between the
steps interfere with a direct comparison, such separating in-betweens
prove nonsensical. We also reject the still-recommended but misleading
stepping-up of the thin layers of water colors or India ink, as explained in
Chapter xx. In order to avoid such mistakes, and also any mechanical
repetition of the too-familiar illustrations of color books, we aim at
a more creative, more challenging, more instructive presentation.
Thus we subdivide and mount our grey scales to show new interactions,
particularly between graduating and non-graduating greys, and
vice versa. (See plate v-1.)
translated_text: 这些剪片应按前述方式排列成渐层。阶差显得越柔和，阶差越均等，研究就越有价值、越有说服力。由于阶差之间的任何线条或空白都会妨碍直接比较，这种分隔性的中间物证明是荒谬的。我们也摒弃那种仍被推荐却具有误导性的做法，即用水彩或印度墨的薄层逐步叠加来形成阶差，如第 xx 章所解释的。为了避免这类错误，也为了避免机械地重复色彩书籍中过于熟悉的插图，我们力求一种更具创造性、更有挑战性、更富教益的呈现方式。因此，我们将灰阶加以细分并装裱，以显示新的相互作用，尤其是渐变灰与非渐变灰之间的相互作用，反之亦然。（见图版 v-1。）

source_text: Color intensity-brightness
translated_text: 色彩强度——亮度

source_text:
After the study of "Lighter or Darker" and with some training
in gradation studies, one can expect to come
translated_text:
在研究了“更亮或更暗”并经过一些
渐层研究训练之后，可以期待达成

source_text: to an agreement on different light intensities.
translated_text: 关于不同光强度的一致意见。

source_text:
However, when it comes to color intensity (brightness),
occasionally one may find agreement among a few people
but hardly within a large group such as a class.
translated_text:
然而，一旦涉及色彩强度（亮度），
有时也许会发现少数人之间意见一致，
但在一个较大的群体，如一个班级之内，则几乎不可能。

source_text:
As "gentlemen prefer blondes," so everyone has preference for certain colors
and prejudices against others. This applies to color combinations as well.
It seems good that we are of different tastes.
translated_text:
正如“绅士偏爱金发女郎”，每个人也都偏爱某些颜色，
并对另一些颜色抱有偏见。这同样适用于色彩组合。
我们拥有不同的品味，这似乎是好事。

source_text:
As it is with people in our daily life, so it is with color.
We change, correct, or reverse our opinions about colors, and this change
of opinion may shift forth and back.
translated_text:
正如我们日常生活中对人的看法一样，色彩也是如此。
我们会改变、修正或推翻自己对颜色的看法，而这种
看法的改变可能来回摇摆。

source_text:
Therefore, we try to recognize our preferences and our aversions-
what colors dominate in our work; what colors, on the other hand,
are rejected, disliked, or of no appeal. Usually a special effort
in using disliked colors ends with our falling in love with them.
translated_text:
因此，我们试着认识自己的偏好和厌恶——
哪些颜色在我们的作品中占主导；另一方面，哪些颜色
被拒绝、不受喜欢，或没有吸引力。通常，在使用不喜欢的颜色上付出特别努力，最终会使我们爱上它们。

source_text:
The exercise in color intensity consists of sorting
all possible shades and tints within a hue. From these is chosen
the most typical hue (the bluest blue, the greenest green, etc.)
and it is placed within the group accordingly. (See plate v-3.)
translated_text:
色彩强度练习包括对一个色相范围内
所有可能的暗调和淡调进行分类。从中选出
最典型的色相（最蓝的蓝、最绿的绿，等等），
并相应地置于该组之中。（见图版 v-3。）

source_text:
1 color appears as 2 -
looking like the reversed grounds
translated_text:
1 种颜色显现为 2 种——
看起来像反转的底色

source_text: VI
translated_text: VI

source_text:
Having presented, in the previous problem, a very detailed explanation
of a step-by-step method of teaching and learning, the following problem
permits a briefer description.
translated_text: 在前一个问题中，我们已经对一种循序渐进的教学与学习方法作了十分详尽的说明，所以下一个问题可以作较为简略的描述。

source_text: With the first exercise in color interaction we make
translated_text: 在第一个色彩相互作用练习中，我们使

source_text: 1 color look like 2, or, what means the same,
translated_text: 1 种颜色看起来像 2 种，或者，意思相同地说，

source_text:
3 colors look like 4. The next step is to make
3 colors look like 2, or, describing it as in the previous task,
translated_text:
使 3 种颜色看起来像 4 种。下一步是使
3 种颜色看起来像 2 种，或者，按前一项任务的说法，

source_text:
I color is to show 2 faces which refer to the 2 colors
of the reversed grounds,
or, the changed color is to echo the 2 changing ones.
translated_text:
1 种颜色要呈现出 2 副面貌，它们指向反转底色的
2 种颜色，
或者说，被改变的颜色要呼应那 2 种发生变化的颜色。

source_text:
After showing a few examples, the task of producing similar effects
is introduced with the question:
translated_text:
展示几个例子之后，便以如下问题引入
产生类似效果的任务：

source_text:
Which color will play simultaneously the roles
of the 2 colors of the 2 reciprocal grounds?
translated_text:
哪一种颜色将同时扮演
2 个相互对应底色的 2 种颜色的角色？

source_text: The first class exhibition of preliminary solutions shows that most of the
translated_text: 第一次课堂展示的初步解答表明，大多数

source_text: trial colors selected appear closer to one ground than to the other.
translated_text: 所选试验色看起来更接近其中一个底色，而不是另一个。

source_text:
However, when one tries to find a color that is equally close
or equally distant from both grounds, one will discover that
even a large collection of color paper (even that of the entire class)
may not provide the fitting tone.
translated_text: 然而，当人们试图找到一种与两种底色同样接近或同样疏远的颜色时，就会发现，即使有大量彩纸（哪怕是全班所有的彩纸），也未必能提供合适的色调。

source_text:
Then, instead of pushing the in-between color to one or the other side,
we must consider changing 1 or both of the grounds, either moving
closer to or more distant from the in-between color. (See diagram.)
translated_text: 于是，与其把这个中间色推向这一边或那一边，我们必须考虑改变一种或两种底色，使其要么更接近这个中间色，要么离它更远。（见图示。）

source_text:
After repeated trials it must be concluded that the only fitting color
is the one which is topologically in the middle of the colors
of the 2 grounds.
translated_text: 经过反复试验，必须得出结论：唯一合适的颜色，就是在拓扑关系上处于两种底色的颜色中间的那一种。

source_text: t
translated_text: t

source_text: The task is to find this middle color.
translated_text: 任务就是找到这个中间色。

source_text: This is relatively easy when the 2 grounds are of the same hue,
translated_text: 当两种底色属于同一色相时，这相对容易，

source_text:
as with a lighter and a darker green ground,
or with a lighter and a darker violet ground.
translated_text: 例如较浅和较深的绿色底色，或较浅和较深的紫色底色。

source_text:
It is a more challenging task to find the middle color
between 2 different hues
but it is particularly interesting when the 2 grounds
are of opposing (complementary) colors. (See plates v1-3 and v1-4.)
translated_text: 在两种不同色相之间找到中间色，是一项更具挑战性的任务；而当两种底色为相对的（互补的）颜色时，则尤其有趣。（见图版 v1-3 和 v1-4。）

source_text:
2 different colors look alike-
subtraction of color
translated_text:
两种不同的颜色看起来相同——
色彩的减除

source_text: VII
translated_text: VII

source_text:
The fact that one and the same color can perform many different roles
is well known and is consciously applied.
translated_text: 同一种颜色能够扮演许多不同的角色，这一事实众所周知，并且被有意识地加以运用。

source_text:
Less well known is the possibility in the previous exercise
of giving a color the look of reversed grounds.
translated_text: 较少为人所知的是，在前一个练习中，有可能使一种颜色呈现出底色反转后的样貌。

source_text:
Still more exciting is the next task, the reverse of the first:
to make 2 different colors look alike.
translated_text: 更令人兴奋的是下一项任务，它是第一项任务的反向：使两种不同的颜色看起来相同。

source_text:
In the first exercise it was learned that the more different
the grounds, the stronger is their changing influence.
translated_text: 在第一个练习中，我们了解到，底色之间的差异越大，它们的改变影响就越强。

source_text: It has been seen that color differences are caused by 2 factors:
translated_text: 我们已经看到，色彩差异由两个因素造成：

source_text: by hue and by light, and in most cases by both at the same time.
translated_text: 由色相和明度造成，而在大多数情况下，则由两者同时造成。

source_text:
Recognizing this, one is able to "push" light and/ or hue,
by the use of contrasts, away from their first appearance
toward the opposite qualities.
Since this amounts virtually to adding opposite qualities,
translated_text: 认识到这一点，人们便能够通过运用对比，将明度和/或色相从其最初的显现“推”开，使其趋向相反的性质。由于这实际上等同于添加相反的性质，

source_text:
it follows that one might achieve parallel effects
by subtracting those qualities not desired.
translated_text: 由此可见，人们也可能通过减除那些不想要的性质，来获得相似的效果。

source_text: This new experience can be achieved first by observing
translated_text: 这种新的经验首先可以通过观察来获得：

source_text:
3 small samples of 3 reds on a white ground.
They will appear first of all-red.
translated_text: 在白色底色上的三小块三种红色样本。它们首先都会显得——红。

source_text: Then when the 3 reds are placed on a ground of another red
translated_text: 随后，当这三种红色被置于另一种红色的底色上时，

source_text:
their differences, which are differences of hue as well as of light,
will become more obvious.
translated_text: 它们之间的差异，即色相和明度上的差异，会变得更加明显。

source_text:
Third, when placed on a red ground equal to 1 of the 3 samples,
only 2 of the reds will "show," and the lost one is absorbed-subtracted.
Repeated similar experiments with adjacent colors will show
that any ground subtracts its own hue from colors which it carries
and therefore influences.
translated_text: 第三，当把它们置于等于3个样本中1个的红色底色上时，只有2个红色会“显现”，而消失的那一个则被吸收——减去了。用相邻色进行反复的类似实验会表明，任何底色都会从其承载并因而影响的颜色中减去自身的色相。

source_text:
Additional experiments with light colors on light grounds
and dark colors on dark grounds prove that the light of a ground
subtracts in the same way that its hue does.
translated_text: 在浅色底色上放置浅色、在深色底色上放置深色的进一步实验，证明底色的明度会以与其色相相同的方式进行减除。

source_text:
From this, it follows that any diversion among colors
in hue as well as in light-dark relationship
can be reduced if not obliterated visually on grounds
of equal qualities.
translated_text: 由此可见，颜色之间在色相以及明暗关系上的任何差异，若置于具有相同性质的底色上，即使不能在视觉上完全消除，也可以被减弱。

source_text:
Such studies provide a broad training in analytical comparison
and usually evoke surprising results, leading the student
translated_text: 这类研究为分析性比较提供了广泛的训练，并且通常会引发令人惊讶的结果，引导学生

source_text: to an intense study of color. (See plates vrr-4, v11-5, and v11-7.)
translated_text: 深入研究色彩。（见图版vrr-4、v11-5和v11-7。）

source_text: Why color deception?-
translated_text: 为什么会有色彩欺骗？——

source_text: after-image, simultaneous contrast
translated_text: 后像，同时对比

source_text: VIII
translated_text: VIII

source_text:
For a better understanding of why colors read differently
from what they really (physically) are, we show now
the cause of most color illusions.
translated_text: 为了更好地理解为什么颜色看起来不同于它们实际（物理上）所是的样子，我们现在展示大多数色彩错觉的成因。

source_text:
In order to prepare for the second part of this demonstration, cut out in
red and white color paper 2 equal circles ( of ca. 3-inch diameter)
and mark their centers with a small black dot.
(See plate vm-1.)
translated_text: 为了准备这一演示的第二部分，用红色和白色彩纸剪出2个相等的圆（直径约3英寸），并用一个小黑点标出它们的中心。（见图版vm-1。）

source_text:
Then paste them-horizontally related-the red circle to
the left and the white one to the right, on the blackboard or
a piece of black paper or black cardboard, ca. 10 inches high and
translated_text: 然后将它们按水平关系粘贴起来——红色圆在左，白色圆在右——贴在黑板上，或一张黑纸或黑卡纸上；黑纸或黑卡纸约10英寸高，

source_text:
20 inches long, with about equal amounts of black before, between,
and after the 2 circles.
translated_text: 20英寸长，在2个圆的前方、之间和后方留出大致相等的黑色区域。

source_text: Now, by staring steadily at the marked center of the red
translated_text: 现在，通过稳定地凝视红色圆上标出的中心，

source_text:
circle ( up to half a minute) one soon discovers how difficult
it is to keep the eye fixed on a point. After a while,
moon-sickle shapes appear, moving along the circle's
periphery. In spite of this, one must continue to focus on
the red center point in order to assure the desired experience.
Then quickly shift the focus to the center of the white circle.
translated_text: （最长半分钟）人们很快会发现，要让眼睛固定在一个点上是多么困难。过一会儿，会出现月牙形的形状，沿着圆的周边移动。尽管如此，仍必须继续聚焦于红色的中心点，以确保获得预期的体验。然后迅速将焦点移到白色圆的中心。

source_text:
From the class one usually hears noises which indicate
surprise or astonishment. This happens because all normal eyes
suddenly see green or blue-green instead of white. This green
translated_text: 通常会从班上听到表示惊讶或惊奇的声音。之所以如此，是因为所有正常的眼睛都会突然看到绿色或蓝绿色，而不是白色。这种绿色

source_text:
is the complementary color of red or red-orange.
The phenomenon of seeing green (in this case) instead of white
is called after-image, or simultaneous contrast.
translated_text: 是红色或橙红色的补色。看到绿色（在此例中）而不是白色的现象，称为后像，或同时对比。

source_text: A plausible explanation:
translated_text: 一种似乎合理的解释：

source_text:
One theory maintains that the nerve ends on the human retina (rods and cones)
are tuned to receive any of the 3 primary colors (red, yellow,
or blue), which constitute all colors.
translated_text: 有一种理论认为，人类视网膜上的神经末梢（视杆细胞和视锥细胞）被调谐为能够接收3种原色（红、黄或蓝）中的任何一种，而这3种原色构成所有颜色。

source_text:
Staring at red will fatigue the red-sensitive parts, so that with
a sudden shift to white (which again consists ofred, yellow, and blue),
only the mixture of yellow and blue occurs. And this is green,
the complement of red.
translated_text: 凝视红色会使对红色敏感的部分疲劳，因此当突然转向白色（白色同样由红、黄、蓝组成）时，只发生黄色和蓝色的混合。而这就是绿色，即红色的补色。

source_text:
The fact that the after-image or simultaneous contrast
is a psycho-physiological phenomenon should prove
that no normal eye, not even the most trained one, is foolproof
against color deception.
He who claims to see colors independent of their illusionary changes
fools only himself, and no one else.
translated_text: 后像或同时对比是一种心理—生理现象，这一事实应当证明，任何正常的眼睛，哪怕是训练最有素的眼睛，也不可能完全不受色彩欺骗的影响。声称自己能够不受颜色错觉性变化影响而看见颜色的人，只是在欺骗自己，而不是别人。

source_text:
Color mixture in paper-
illusion of transparence
translated_text:
纸上的色彩混合——
透明感的错觉

source_text: IX
translated_text: IX

source_text:
It is obvious that in working with color paper there is no way
of mixing the colors mechanically, as paint and pigment permit,
and as they invite one to do on a palette or in a container.
translated_text: 显而易见，在使用彩色纸时，不可能像颜料和色料所允许的那样，以机械方式混合颜色；颜料和色料还会诱使人在调色板上或容器中这样做。

source_text:
Though this may first appear as a handicap, it is actually a challenge
to study color mixture in our imagination, that is, so to say,
with closed eyes.
translated_text: 尽管这起初可能显得是一种障碍，但实际上它是一项挑战，要求我们在想象中研究色彩混合，也就是说，可以说，是闭着眼睛来研究。

source_text:
Starting with the simple and well-known fact that blue and yellow
when mixed produce green, a blue and yellow are selected
and held next to each other. One tries to imagine what kind of green
would result from a mixture of these 2 colors.
Then a paper is selected appropriate to this imagined mixture.
translated_text: 从一个简单而众所周知的事实出发：蓝色和黄色混合会产生绿色。选取一张蓝纸和一张黄纸，并将它们并置。人们试着想象这两种颜色混合后会产生什么样的绿色。然后选取一张与这一想象中的混合色相适合的纸。

source_text:
In order to find out whether the "thought-out" mixture is acceptable-
believable-convincing-the 3 colors (2 "color parents" and
translated_text: 为了弄清这种“想出来的”混合是否可以接受——可信——有说服力——这3种颜色（2个“色彩父母”和

source_text: 1 "color descendant") are placed in 3 equal rectangles as follows:
translated_text: 1个“色彩后代”）按如下方式置于3个相等的矩形中：

source_text:
Blue horizontally (1), green vertically (2)
so that its upper part overlaps the blue. The yellow is put on top
of the green (3) so that its top edge coincides with the bottom edge of the blue.
translated_text: 蓝色横向放置（1），绿色纵向放置（2），使其上部与蓝色重叠。黄色放在绿色之上（3），使其上边缘与蓝色的下边缘重合。

source_text:
In such placement, the green will be the "in-between" of the other colors
and thus their mixture.
translated_text: 在这样的放置中，绿色将成为另外两种颜色的“中间项”，因而也就是它们的混合色。

source_text:
After the class has found several believable mixtures, these are collected
for an exhibition (most practically, on the floor) and the most convincing ones
are selected. Some are usually more successful than others. The class states
their merits and shortcomings and suggests possible corrections and improvements.
translated_text: 全班找到若干可信的混合色之后，将它们收集起来作一次展示（最实际的做法是在地板上），并选出最有说服力的作品。有些通常比另一些更成功。全班陈述它们的优点和缺点，并提出可能的修正和改进。

source_text:
By means of the exhibition, the students will be reminded that there are many blues
and many yellows, and will conclude that there are innumerable mixtures
descending from them. It is obvious that any 2 colors can produce many mixtures.
translated_text: 通过这次展示，学生会被提醒：蓝色有许多种，黄色也有许多种；并会得出结论：由它们衍生出的混合色不可胜数。显而易见，任意2种颜色都能产生许多混合色。

source_text:
In addition to the illusion of mixture, another deception will be recognized-
that, in an illusionary mixture in paper, 1 color seems to show
through the other. The "mixture" paper, therefore, loses its opacity and
appears transparent or translucent.
translated_text: 除了混合的错觉之外，还会认识到另一种欺骗——在纸上形成的错觉性混合中，1种颜色似乎透过另一种颜色显现出来。因此，“混合”纸失去了它的不透明性，显得透明或半透明。

source_text:
In order to make the eye read this double illusion of mixture and of
transparence, the colors must be placed in overlapping shapes.
translated_text: 为了使眼睛读出这种关于混合和透明性的双重错觉，颜色必须放置在相互重叠的形状中。

source_text:
In the drawing on page 26 the hatched parts belong to each of the overlapping
shapes and are therefore the logical place for the mixture.
translated_text: 在第26页的图中，带阴影的部分属于每一个相互重叠的形状，因此是混合色的合乎逻辑的位置。

source_text: After simple mixtures, such as blue and yellow producing green-red and
translated_text: 在简单的混合之后，例如蓝色和黄色产生绿色——红色和

source_text:
blue producing violet-black and white producing grey-less common
pairs, such as pink and ochre, present a further challenge.
translated_text: 蓝色产生紫色——黑色和白色产生灰色——不那么常见的配对，如粉红色和赭色，则提出了进一步的挑战。

source_text:
For a more intensive experience, keep the area of the mixture
larger than those of the 2 mixing ones. (See plate 1x-1.)
translated_text: 为了获得更强烈的体验，应使混合色的面积大于2种进行混合的颜色的面积。（见图版1x-1。）

then our first task is to find C's, which are mixtures of A and B,

Color light, or direct color, probably is most familiar

The scientific analysis of the physical qualities (wave length, etc.)

When he mixes his colors, he projects them on a screen,

source_text:
By means of a prismatic lens, the physicist easily demonstrates
that the color spectrum of the rainbow is a dispersion of the white sunlight.
With this he proves also that the sum of all colors in light is white.
This demonstrates an additive mixture.

这表明了一种加法混合。

source_text:
b)
When pigment or paint is mixed on a palette or in a container
it is seen by the eye as reflected light.
This mixing will never result in white as the sum of colors.
On the contrary, the more color that is mixed, the more the mixture approaches
a dark grey leaning toward black. This we call subtractive mixture.
Also, the psychologist, who mixes colors of reflecting colorants
optically on the rotating wheel, is not able to arrive at mixtures
lighter than the lighter color parent of the mixture.
translated_text:
b)

translated_text: XI 透明与空间幻觉

source_text: Color boundaries and plastic action
translated_text: 色彩边界与造型作用

source_text: A study of color mixture in paper leads to 3 important discoveries.
translated_text: 纸上色彩混合研究带来三个重要发现。

source_text: First, under normal conditions, a subtractive mixture is not as light
translated_text: 首先，在正常条件下，减法混合并不如

source_text:
as the lighter of the color parents nor as dark as the darker one.
Furthermore, the mixture is reciprocally neither higher nor lower
in color intensity than the color parents.
translated_text:
既不如颜色母体中较浅者那样浅，也不如较深者那样深。
此外，这种混合在色彩强度上相对于颜色母体而言，既不更高也不更低。

source_text:
Second, a mixture depends upon the proportion in which colors are mixed.
Varying amounts of blue and yellow, for instance, define the character
of a green. This indicates a possible predominance of 1 color parent.
translated_text:
第二，混合取决于各种颜色混合时的比例。
例如，不同量的蓝色和黄色决定了一种绿色的特征。
这表明某一个颜色母体可能占据优势。

source_text:
Third, when 1 color is read as appearing above or below another
in the transparence studies, a third deception is recognized-space-illusion.
translated_text: 第三，当在透明性研究中一种颜色被读作显现于另一种颜色之上或之下时，便可辨认出第三种错觉——空间错觉。

source_text:
This leads to the next task:
To produce different illusionary mixtures which derive from 1 pair
of parent colors. If the parents are again a blue and a yellow,
some greens will be found with yellow dominance
and others with blue dominance. With more mixing experience
it will become apparent that the nearness of a mixture to one side
translated_text:
这引出了下一项任务：
用一对母体色产生不同的错觉性混合。如果母体色仍是一种蓝色和一种黄色，
就会发现有些绿色以黄色为主导，
另一些则以蓝色为主导。随着混合经验的增加，
会变得明显的是，一种混合色越接近一侧

source_text:
(let us say yellow) necessitates distance from the opposite side
(in this case blue).
translated_text:
（比如说黄色），就必然越远离相反的一侧
（在此例中为蓝色）。

source_text: After having found several mixtures of different pairs of parent colors,
translated_text: 在找到若干对不同母体色的几种混合之后，

source_text:
we then try to find the most significant and the most difficult mixture
-the middle mixture. Topographically, this middle mixture demands

——中间混合。从拓扑位置上说，这种中间混合要求

Such efforts forth and back in our search for a middle color-

source_text:
Besides an explanation of the above diagrams on the blackboard,
a physical demonstration in space may clarify this further.
When discussing the first trial studies, exhibited on the floor
with the students standing around them, 2 hands held horizontally
translated_text: 除了在黑板上解释上述图示之外，在空间中作一次实体演示也许能进一步说明这一点。在讨论最初的试验性习作时，把它们展示在地板上，学生们围站在周围，两只手水平举着，

1 above the other may act as the 2 outer colors.
And a third hand held between them may demonstrate various possibilities
of color selection and placement, either by moving the hand indicating
the middle color up or down, or by moving the outer hands up
and/ or down, singly or together.
translated_text: 一只在另一只上方，可以充当两个外侧色彩。第三只手举在二者之间，则可以演示色彩选择和位置安排的各种可能性：或者上下移动表示中间色彩的那只手，或者将外侧的两只手单独或一起向上和/或向下移动。

source_text:
With a more developed sensitivity for mixtures, it will be discovered
that distance, nearness, and equidistance between colors
can be recognized through the boundaries between the mixture and the mixture parents.
translated_text: 随着对混合更为发展的敏感性，人们会发现，色彩之间的距离、接近以及等距，可以通过混合色与混合色的母色之间的边界来辨认。

source_text:
By exercising comparison and distinction of color boundaries, a new and
important measure is gained for the reading of the plastic action of color,
that is, for the spatial organization of color.
Since softer boundaries disclose nearness implying connection,
harder boundaries indicate distance, separation.
translated_text: 通过练习比较和辨别色彩边界，我们获得了一种新的、重要的尺度，用以解读色彩的造型作用，也就是解读色彩的空间组织。由于较柔和的边界显示接近，意味着联系；较坚硬的边界则表明距离、分离。

source_text:
In both interpretations colors are placed above or below each other,
or in front of or behind each other. They are read as here and there,
as over, and beyond there, and therefore in space.
translated_text: 在这两种解读中，色彩被置于彼此的上方或下方，或置于彼此的前方或后方。它们被读作此处与彼处，被读作在……之上，以及在彼处之外，因而是在空间之中。

source_text: All this seems to change with colors producing middle mixtures. Sometimes
translated_text: 所有这一切在产生中间混合色的色彩那里似乎发生了变化。有时

source_text:
they appear as if meeting within a 2-dimensional plane; at other times
they can be read-interchangeably-as higher or lower than the mixture.
translated_text: 它们仿佛在一个二维平面内相遇；另一些时候，它们又可以被解读为——并且可以互换地被解读为——高于或低于混合色。

source_text:
Thus, with a middle mixture all boundaries are equally soft or hard.
As a consequence, a middle mixture appears frontal, as a color by itself.
This is comparable to the reading of any symmetrical order
and the middle mixture will behave unspatially,
unless its own shape, or surrounding shapes, decides differently.
(See plates x1-1 and x1-3.)
translated_text: 因此，对于一个中间混合色而言，所有边界都同样柔和或同样坚硬。其结果是，中间混合色显得正面呈现，像一种自足的色彩。这可与对任何对称秩序的解读相比；中间混合色将表现得不具空间性，除非它自身的形状，或周围的形状，作出不同的决定。（见图版 x1-1 和 x1-3。）

source_text:
Such a study, or a similar recognition, in my opinion, led Cezanne
to his unique and new articulation in painting. He was the first
to develop color areas which produce both distinct and indistinct endings
-areas connected and unconnected-areas with and without boundaries-
translated_text: 在我看来，正是这样的研究，或类似的认识，引导塞尚走向他在绘画中独特而崭新的表达。他是第一个发展出这样一些色彩区域的人：它们既产生明确的端点，也产生不明确的端点——相连的区域与不相连的区域——有边界的区域与无边界的区域——

source_text: as means of plastic organization.
translated_text: 作为造型组织的手段。

source_text:
And, in order to prevent evenly painted areas from looking flat and frontal,
he used emphasized borders sparingly, mainly where he needed
a spatial separation from adjacent color areas.
translated_text: 并且，为了防止均匀涂绘的区域显得平面而正面，他很克制地使用强调的边缘，主要是在他需要与相邻色彩区域形成空间分离之处。

source_text: XII Optical mixture-after-image revised
translated_text: XII 视觉混合——后像修订

source_text: XIII The Bezold Effect
translated_text: XIII 贝佐尔德效应

source_text: In contrast to after-image, so far the main concern of our studies, here
translated_text: 与迄今为止我们的研究主要关注的后像相对，这里

source_text:
is another very different color illusion called "optical mixture."
Instead of 2 (or more) colors changing each other, "pulling" or "pushing"
each other into different appearances (toward both greater difference and greater
translated_text: 是另一种十分不同的色彩错觉，称为“视觉混合”。在这里，并不是两个（或更多）色彩彼此改变，把彼此“拉”或“推”向不同的外观（既朝向更大的差异，也朝向更大的

source_text:
similarity), here 2 colors (or more), perceived simultaneously, are seen
combined and thus merged into 1 new color. In this process, the 2
original colors are first annulled and made invisible, and then replaced by
translated_text: 相似），而是两个（或更多）同时被感知的色彩被看作结合在一起，从而融合成一种新的色彩。在这一过程中，两个原有色彩首先被抵消并变得不可见，随后被

source_text: a substitute called optical mixture.
translated_text: 一种称为视觉混合的替代物所取代。

source_text:
From the Impressionist painters we have learned that they never presented, let us say,
green by itself. Instead of using green paint mixed mechanically from yellow
and blue, they applied yellow and blue unmixed in small dots, so that they
became mixed only in our perception-as an impression. That the dots
mentioned were small indicates that this effect depends on size and on distance.
translated_text: 从印象派画家那里我们了解到，他们从不呈现，比如说，单独的绿色。他们不是使用由黄色和蓝色机械混合而成的绿色颜料，而是把未混合的黄色和蓝色以小点的形式施加上去，使它们只在我们的感知中混合——作为一种印象。上述小点之所以小，说明这种效果取决于尺寸和距离。

source_text:
The discovery of the mixing of colors in our perception led in the last
century not only to the new painting technique of the Impressionists, and
particularly of the Pointillists, but also to the invention of new photomechanical
reproduction techniques, the 3- and 4-color process for paintings, and the
halftone process for black-and-white pictures. In the first case, 3 or 4
color plates subdivided into tiny printing dots mix to innumerable color
translated_text: 上个世纪，色彩在我们的感知中发生混合这一发现，不仅导致了印象派，尤其是点彩派的新绘画技法，也导致了新的照相机械复制技术的发明：用于绘画复制的三色和四色制版法，以及用于黑白图像的网目调制版法。在第一种情况下，分解成细小印刷网点的三块或四块色版，混合成无数的色调

source_text: shades and tints. In the second case, a plate for black also subdivided by
translated_text: 和明度层次。在第二种情况下，一块用于黑色的版也经由

source_text:
a screen in tiny dots mixes with the white paper in just as innumerable
tones of white-grey-black.
translated_text: 网屏分解为细小网点，与白纸混合，形成同样无数的白—灰—黑调子。

source_text:
There is a special kind of optical mixture, the Bezold Effect, named after its
discoverer, Wilhelm von Bezold (1837-1907). He recognized
this effect when searching for a method through which he could change the
color combinations of his rug designs entirely by adding or changing 1 color only.
Apparently, there is so far no clear recognition of the optical-
translated_text: 有一种特殊的光学混合，即贝佐尔德效应，以其发现者威廉·冯·贝佐尔德（1837—1907）命名。他在寻找一种方法时认识到这种效应；通过这种方法，他只需添加或改变一种颜色，便能彻底改变其地毯设计的色彩组合。显然，迄今为止，对于其中所涉及的光学-

source_text: perceptual conditions involved. (See plates x1rr-1, x111-2, and xm-3.)
translated_text: 知觉条件尚无清晰的认识。（见图版 x1rr-1、x111-2 和 xm-3。）

Color intervals and
transformation
translated_text:
色彩间隔与
转换

source_text: XIV
translated_text: XIV

source_text:
The tune of "Good morning to you" consists of 4 tones. It can be sung
in a high soprano, a low basso, and in all in-between voices, as well as
on many levels and in many keys. It can be played on innumerable instruments.
translated_text: 《早上好》的曲调由4个音组成。它可以由高音女声、低音男声以及其间所有声部来演唱，也可以在许多音域和许多调上演唱。它可以由无数种乐器演奏。

source_text:
In all possible ways of performance, this melody will keep its character
and it will be recognized instantly.
translated_text: 在所有可能的表演方式中，这一旋律都会保持其特征，并会立刻被辨认出来。

source_text:
Why? The intervals of the 4 tones, that is, their acoustical
constellation (again comparable with a topographical relationship),
remains the same.
translated_text: 为什么？这4个音的间隔，即它们的声学星座关系（同样可与地形关系相比），保持不变。

source_text:
Although it is not common practice, one can also speak of intervals
between colors.
Colors and hues are defined, as are tones in music, by wave length.
translated_text:
虽然这并非常见做法，但人们也可以谈论色彩之间的间隔。
颜色和色相与音乐中的音一样，都是由波长来界定的。

source_text:
Any color (shade or tint) always has 2 decisive characteristics:
color intensity (brightness) and light intensity (lightness).
Therefore, color intervals also have this double-sidedness, this duality.
translated_text:
任何颜色（暗色或淡色）始终具有2个决定性特征：
色彩强度（明度）和光强度（亮度）。
因此，色彩间隔也具有这种双面性、这种二重性。

source_text:
As has been stated before, after some training one might easily agree
on light relationship, that is, which of 2 colors is lighter
and which is darker. However, there is rarely agreement on color intensity,
that is, which among a number of reds is the reddest red.
For this reason the interval transformation exercise is concerned mainly
with light intensity.
translated_text:
如前所述，经过一些训练，人们或许很容易就光的关系达成一致，即两种颜色中哪一种较亮、哪一种较暗。然而，对于色彩强度，即在若干种红色中哪一种是最红的红色，却很少能达成一致。
因此，间隔转换练习主要关涉光强度。

source_text:
To prepare a basic exercise in color transformation, combine
4 equal squares of different colors to make 1 larger square.
Within this grouping of 4 squares, the lighter will differentiate
from the heavier, darker color. Therefore, the squares will connect
with each other or separate according to contrast and affinity,
as vertical, horizontal, or diagonal pairs, or as a trio forming
an angle, embracing or opposing a fourth square. (See diagrams.)
translated_text:
为准备一项色彩转换的基础练习，将4个不同颜色的等大正方形组合成1个较大的正方形。
在这4个正方形的组合中，较亮的颜色会与较重、较暗的颜色区分开来。因此，这些正方形会依照对比和亲和关系彼此连接或分离，形成垂直、水平或对角的成对关系，或形成一个构成角度的三元组，包围或对立于第四个正方形。（见图示。）

source_text: The task is to transfer these specific relationships to a higher or lower key
translated_text: 任务是把这些特定关系转移到更高或更低的调中

source_text:
within 2 or more groups of equally large rectangles. Of course,
if the first group contains the darkest color available, one cannot go lower.
Similarly, the lightest white would not permit any transference to
translated_text: 在2组或更多组同样大小的矩形之内。当然，如果第一组包含了可获得的最暗颜色，就无法再降低。类似地，最亮的白色也不允许任何向

source_text: a higher key.
translated_text: 更高调的转移。

source_text:
It is rarely possible to retain the first 4 rectangles selected.
Frequently it will be impossible to find 4 colors equally raised
or lowered when compared with the original set. If so, the original set
should be changed in order to transfer more successfully.
translated_text: 很少能够保留最初选定的4个矩形。常常不可能找到4种相对于原组同等提高或降低的颜色。若是如此，就应改变原组，以便更成功地进行转移。

source_text: In a successful study, both groups should show equal relationships
translated_text: 在一项成功的习作中，两组应显示出相等的关系

source_text: in equal placement, as a constellation. Then, as with the study of
translated_text: 在相等的放置中，作为一种星座关系。然后，如同在

source_text: varying mixtures, the boundaries between the 4 rectangles
translated_text: 变化混合的研究中一样，4个矩形之间的边界

source_text: will also appear similar in both groups.
translated_text: 在两组中也会显得相似。

source_text:
Again, the aim of this exercise is not to present a pleasant, perhaps harmonious look,
but to present a study aiming at one distinct relationship-
translated_text:
同样，这一练习的目的并不是呈现一种悦目的、也许和谐的外观，
而是呈现一项旨在建立一种明确关系的研究——

source_text: parallel intervals.
translated_text: 平行间隔。

source_text:
How do we prove such similarity, such parallelism?
As has been learned from gradation studies done at the beginning, it is
translated_text:
我们如何证明这种相似性、这种平行性？
正如从一开始所做的渐变研究中已经学到的，

source_text:
poor "psychological engineering" to present the gradation steps
unconnected, that is, separated by black lines. Similarly, in the transformation
translated_text: 把渐变步骤呈现为彼此不相连，也就是说，用黑线隔开，是拙劣的“心理工程”。同样，在转换

source_text:
exercise it is hard to compare the boundaries within the
original group of 4 rectangles with the raised or lowered boundaries in
the second, separated group.
translated_text: 练习中，也难以把原来一组4个矩形内部的边界与第二组、分隔开的一组中升高或降低的边界进行比较。

source_text:
The only way in which the 2 groups can be compared easily and accurately
is to superimpose I group on the other.
translated_text: 要容易而准确地比较这2组，唯一的方法是把一组叠置在另一组之上。

source_text:
For this purpose we cut from the center of the first group
a small rectangle and exchange it with an equally shaped and placed
small rectangle of the second group. (See diagrams below.)
translated_text: 为此，我们从第一组的中心剪下一个小矩形，并把它与第二组中形状和位置相同的一个小矩形互换。（见下图。）

source_text:
Immediately, the superimposed rectangles will show
whether the stepping up or down within I group corresponds
with the stepping in the other. A further comparison should be made
between each small rectangle and the larger group beneath it.
The sample studies will also show that the boundaries provide
an important means of comparison.
translated_text: 这样，叠置的矩形会立即显示，一组内部的升阶或降阶是否与另一组中的阶进相对应。还应在每个小矩形与其下方较大的组之间作进一步比较。样例研究还会表明，边界提供了一种重要的比较手段。

source_text:
Usually, as shown, a lower color tetrachord is transferred
to a higher key, or opposite; one may also break with habit and
try to make a low color constellation still lower, or a high one
still higher. (See plates XIV-I, XIV-2, and xrv-3.)
translated_text: 通常，如图所示，是把一个较低的色彩四音列转调到较高的调上，或反过来；也可以打破习惯，尝试使一个低的色彩星群更低，或使一个高的色彩星群更高。（见图版XIV-1、XIV-2和XIV-3。）

source_text:
By keeping the stepping-up or down-small, a special effect of
transparence is achieved called film color, to be described in Chapter xvrr.
translated_text: 通过使升阶或降阶保持得很小，可以获得一种特殊的透明效果，称为薄膜色，将在第XVII章加以说明。

source_text:
The middle mixture again-
intersecting colors
translated_text:
再次讨论中间混合——
交 intersecting colors

source_text: xv
translated_text: XV

source_text:
Our studies of illusionary transparence have shown how difficult it is
to find a middle mixture.
translated_text: 我们对错觉性透明的研究已经表明，要找到一种中间混合是多么困难。

source_text:
A true middle mixture is distinguished by being equidistant
-in light and in hue-
from either mixture parent.
translated_text: 真正的中间混合，其特点是它在明度和色相上与任一混合母色等距。

source_text:
Unfortunately, for an untrained eye, it is hard to recognize
such equidistance.
We have seen that the color boundaries between the mixing color
and the mixed one have proved to be helpful measures.
translated_text: 遗憾的是，对未经训练的眼睛来说，很难辨认这种等距。我们已经看到，混合色与被混合色之间的色彩边界已证明是有帮助的衡量依据。

source_text: The purpose of the new problem, intersecting colors,
translated_text: 新的课题，即交 intersecting colors，目的在于

source_text: is to show and to produce a certain constellation
translated_text: 显示并产生某种星群，

source_text: by which even an untrained eye will recognize
translated_text: 借此，即使未经训练的眼睛也能辨认出

source_text:
within a mixture not only the constituents
but also their respective amounts within that mixture.
translated_text: 一种混合之中不仅有哪些构成成分，而且还能辨认出这些成分在该混合中的各自含量。

source_text: For an initial experience in this direction
translated_text: 作为朝这一方向迈出的初步经验，

source_text:
find 3 equally large sheets of 1 red in 3 shades,
a light red, the same red darker, and the almost always elusive
middle mixture of these reds. Or, if not available in red,
translated_text: 找3张同样大小的纸，都是同一种红色但有3种深浅：一种浅红、同一种红色的较深色，以及这些红色那种几乎总是难以捉摸的中间混合。或者，如果红色中找不到，

source_text: take any other color providing a lighter, a middle, and
translated_text: 就取任何其他颜色，只要它提供一种较浅、一种中间以及

source_text: a darker shade or tint. (See diagrams, next page.)
translated_text: 一种较深的色度或淡色。（见下一页图示。）

source_text:
Place them adjacent to one another,
with the lighter red to the left and overlapped by the edge of the middle red;
translated_text: 把它们彼此相邻放置，较浅的红色在左，并让中间红色的边缘叠压其上；

source_text:
then place the dark red on top of the middle red, allowing only a narrow strip
of the middle red ( about ¼ inch wide) to remain visible.
translated_text: 然后把深红色放在中间红色上面，只让中间红色的一条窄带（约¼英寸宽）仍然可见。

source_text:
Then, very slowly, pull the dark sheet to the right,
gradually making the narrow strip of the middle red wider.
translated_text: 然后，极其缓慢地将深色纸片向右拉，逐渐使中间红色的狭窄条带变宽。

source_text:
By staring at the middle red, observe that the wider it grows, the more it appears
not as 1 but as 2 colors, becoming lighter and lighter
at the right edge, and, at the same time, darker and darker
at the left edge.
translated_text: 凝视中间的红色，观察到它越变宽，就越不像是1种颜色，而像是2种颜色：右边缘变得越来越浅，同时，左边缘变得越来越深。
